docs.title: Agentic AI for Smart Procurement in Manufacturing Industries
docs.text:
Status: Production Ready Architecture: Multi-Agent Microservices Framework: Next.js + FastAPI + Kafka Human-In-The-Loop: Enabled

Welcome to the centralized technical documentation for ProcureFlow, an autonomous multi-agent procurement platform designed specifically for manufacturing industries.

docs.title: 📌 Executive Summary
docs.text:
Manufacturing procurement involves document processing, inventory assessment, vendor selection, purchase-order generation, approvals, and risk analysis. Traditional manual and rule-based approaches render these activities time-consuming, siloed, and prone to costly delays.

ProcureFlow provides an intelligent, AI-driven procurement management solution using a modular multi-agent architecture. Specialized agents coordinate document intelligence (OCR), real-time inventory gap detection, multi-attribute vendor evaluation, automated purchase order generation, risk mitigation, and digital signatures—while retaining strict human oversight for financial approvals and contract execution.

docs.title: 🚀 Key System Capabilities
docs.text:
• :material-file-document-check:{ .lg .middle } Document Intelligence & OCR

    Automated invoice, PO, and requisition ingestion using advanced Optical Character Recognition and LLM parsing to extract structured line items without manual data entry.

  • :material-warehouse:{ .lg .middle } Inventory Analysis & Shortage Detection

    Monitors enterprise stock across multiple warehouse databases to identify real-time shortages against reorder thresholds and bills of materials.

  • :material-account-star:{ .lg .middle } Multi-Attribute Vendor Scoring

    Dynamically ranks suppliers using historical delivery accuracy, quality ratings, unit pricing, compliance scores, and real-time reliability metrics.

  • :material-shield-alert:{ .lg .middle } Proactive Risk Assessment

    Evaluates market price volatility, single-supplier concentration risk, lead-time variance, and geopolitical risk factors before placing orders.

  • :material-draw-pen:{ .lg .middle } Tiered Approvals & DocuSign Integration

    Automated routing of requisitions based on enterprise financial authority thresholds, coupled with cryptographic digital signatures and DocuSign verification.

  • :material-robot:{ .lg .middle } RAG-Powered Vendor Chatbot

    LLM-powered conversational interface that allows suppliers to query order status, clarify delivery schedules, and conduct automated RFP negotiations.

docs.title: Specialized Agent Specifications
docs.text: Detailed documentation of each AI agent operating within the ProcureFlow ecosystem, including prompts, toolkits, inputs, outputs, and interface screenshots.

docs.title: 1. Document Intelligence Agent
docs.text:
• Role: Extracts unstructured text and tabular line items from invoices, bills of materials (BOM), and receipts.
  • Tools: Tesseract OCR, PyMuPDF, Vision LLM parsing, Pydantic Schema Validator.
  • Input: Raw PDF or image file uploaded to MinIO.
  • Output: Structured JSON schema with normalized items, unit prices, taxes, and confidence scores.

docs.title: 2. Inventory Analysis Agent
docs.text:
• Role: Evaluates material requests against live multi-warehouse stocks to detect deficits and calculate required procurement quantities.
  • Tools: PostgreSQL Read Connector, Safety Stock Evaluator, Reorder Point (ROP) Calculator.
  • Input: List of required line items with quantities.
  • Output: Net shortage report with urgency rating (Critical, High, Medium, Low).

docs.title: 3. Vendor Evaluation Agent
docs.text:
• Role: Computes multi-attribute weighted rankings for all vendors capable of supplying the identified shortages.
  • Scoring Formula: $$\text{Score} = (w_p \cdot \text{PriceScore}) + (w_d \cdot \text{DeliveryScore}) + (w_q \cdot \text{QualityScore}) + (w_c \cdot \text{ComplianceScore})$$
  • Tools: Historical Performance Query Tool, Catalog Pricing Lookup.
  • Input: Part numbers, deficit quantities, delivery deadline.
  • Output: Ranked vendor shortlist with pricing, lead times, and rationales.

docs.title: 4. Risk Assessment Agent
docs.text:
• Role: Evaluates supply chain risks, supplier dependency concentrations, price volatility, and geopolitical factors before committing purchase orders.
  • Tools: Volatility Index Estimator, Single-Source Dependency Detector, Lead-Time Variance Calculator.
  • Input: Top-ranked vendor profiles and order valuation.
  • Output: Composite Risk Index (Low, Medium, High) with mitigation suggestions.

docs.title: 5. Approval Coordinator Agent
docs.text:
• Role: Enforces corporate financial delegation rules, routes orders to authorized managers, and manages the DocuSign signature lifecycle.
  • Tools: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) Verifier, DocuSign eSignature API Client, Email Notification Dispatcher.
  • Input: Purchase order draft, composite risk score, approver identity.
  • Output: Signed legal contract, audit timestamp, and state transition to PO_EXECUTED.

docs.title: 6. RAG Vendor Chatbot Agent
docs.text:
• Role: Provides 24/7 conversational support for suppliers regarding order status, delivery timelines, payment terms, and automated RFP queries.
  • Architecture: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) using FAISS vector store over purchase orders and vendor contract documents.
  • Tools: Vector Search Tool, PO Status Query Tool, FAQ Knowledge Retrieval.

docs.title: 7. Continuous Feedback & System Learning
docs.text:
ProcureFlow implements a continuous learning loop where procurement managers can submit feedback on agent recommendations:

Feedback scores are stored and used to adjust vendor ranking weights and risk sensitivities dynamically.

docs.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration & System Intelligence
docs.text: ProcureFlow replaces rigid monoliths with a multi-agent collaborative intelligence framework. Rather than relying on a single prompt or monolithic script, specialized agents work cooperatively to solve complex procurement problems.

docs.title: 💡 Key Architectural Principles of the Agents
1. Separation of Concerns
docs.text: Each agent possesses dedicated system instructions, toolkits, and schemas. For instance, the Inventory Agent has SQL read tools for warehouse schemas, while the Risk Assessment Agent utilizes mathematical variance estimators and market indices.

docs.title: 2. Event-Driven Asynchrony
docs.text:
Agents communicate via Apache Kafka topics: - procureflow.document.ingested - procureflow.inventory.shortage - procureflow.vendor.scored - procureflow.risk.evaluated - procureflow.approval.status

This event-driven model guarantees that if one agent encounters a network delay (e.g. external supplier API latency), downstream tasks do not freeze, and state transitions remain resilient.

docs.title: 3. State Management & Ephemeral Memory
docs.text: Active agent sessions and multi-step reasoning traces are stored in Redis. This allows agents to recall previous turns during negotiation, maintain context across large documents, and support idempotency.

docs.title: 4. Human-in-the-Loop Safeguards
docs.text: AI agents produce recommendations, not unilateral commitments. All financial commitments and legal dispatches require human sign-off via the Approval Hub.

docs.text: Data Flow Diagrams depict how data travels through the ProcureFlow platform, detailing input sources, processing checkpoints, persistent datastores, and generated system outputs.

docs.title: 📈 Complete System DFD
docs.text: The following diagram illustrates the multi-stage data flow across external actors, specialized agents, datastores, and approval entities:

docs.title: 🌐 Level 0: Context Diagram
docs.text:
The Context Diagram defines the system boundary and identifies external entities that interact with ProcureFlow.

graph LR
    P[Procurement Manager] -->|1. Upload Invoices & Requisitions| SYS((ProcureFlow System))
    SYS -->|2. Recommendation & Risk Analysis| P
    P -->|3. Financial Approval & Digital Signature| SYS

    INV_DEPT[Warehouse / Inventory Systems] -->|4. Stock Levels & Reorder Triggers| SYS

    SYS -->|5. Purchase Orders & RFPs| VEND[Manufacturing Vendors & Suppliers]

    BOT <--> SYS

    SYS -->|8. Audit Trails & Financial Exports| FIN[Finance & ERP Systems]

docs.title: External Entities
docs.text:
1. Procurement Manager / Approvers: Uploads source procurement requests, reviews agent recommendations, and executes legal/financial authorizations.
  2. Warehouse / Inventory Systems: Streams inventory updates, consumption logs, and bills of materials (BOMs).
  3. Vendors & Suppliers: Receives purchase orders, submits quotations, and interacts with the automated vendor chatbot.
  4. Finance & ERP: Consumes finalized purchase orders, 3-way matching records, and compliance audit logs.

docs.title: Database Architecture & Entity-Relationship (ER) Diagram
docs.text: ProcureFlow employs a robust relational schema in PostgreSQL coupled with MinIO object storage for unstructured document payloads (PDF invoices, scanned POs, and digital signature envelopes).

docs.title: 📊 Entity–Relationship Diagram
docs.text: The core business entities and their relational constraints are mapped below:

docs.title: 1. Document & Ingestion Models
docs.text:
• documents: Tracks raw uploaded files, file sizes, MIME types, and MinIO storage URIs.
  • extracted_line_items: Contains items parsed by the OCR and Document Intelligence agent. Includes extracted product name, SKU, unit count, price, tax breakdown, and parsing confidence score.

docs.title: 2. Multi-Warehouse Inventory Models
docs.text:
• warehouses: Manufacturing facilities and storage depot locations.
  • inventory_items: Current physical stock, reorder point (ROP), safety stock limits, and active allocation counts.
  • stock_movements: Complete ledger of inward material receipts, production issues, and return dispatches.

docs.title: 3. Vendor Master & Performance Scoring
docs.text:
• vendors: Supplier profile, contact person, payment terms, and active operational status.
  • vendor_performance: Aggregated performance metrics including historical on-time delivery rate, quality compliance percentage, defect count, and average fulfillment lead time.
  • vendor_catalogs: Approved pricing tables and lead time matrices per SKU.

docs.title: 4. Purchase Order & Financial Governance
docs.text:
• purchase_orders: Purchase order state machine (Draft, In Review, Approved, Dispatched, Fulfilled, Cancelled). Tracks total valuation, currency, targeted supplier, and approval tier.
  • po_line_items: Granular itemized specifications, negotiated unit rates, and quantity breakdowns.
  • approval_records: Immutable audit logs of managerial approvals, digital signatures, DocuSign envelope IDs, and cryptographic timestamps.

docs.title: 🔌 Data Source Integrations & API Connectors
docs.text: ProcureFlow supports dynamic database connectors and external API integrations, allowing manufacturing enterprises to ingest live ERP inventories and vendor catalogs without manual data exports.

docs.title: Uploading External Database Snapshots
docs.text: Users can directly connect API endpoints or upload structured CSV/SQL database dumps to hydrate initial inventory baselines and vendor catalogs.

docs.title: 🛡️ ACID Guarantees & Audit Integrity
docs.text:
1. Transactional Safety: Critical purchase order state transitions utilize atomic database transactions. If an approval fails or DocuSign webhook throws a communication error, the state automatically rolls back.
  2. Kafka Event Sync: Every database mutation emits a change-data-capture event into Apache Kafka, ensuring downstream reporting microservices and audit logs remain synchronized in real time.

docs.title: System Architecture & Technical Topology
docs.text: ProcureFlow is built on an enterprise-grade, event-driven microservices architecture that separates presentation, agent orchestration, asynchronous task processing, data storage, and external integrations.

docs.title: 🏛️ High-Level Architectural Diagram
docs.text:
The platform is designed around loose coupling, allowing individual agents to execute independently or collaborate via an event bus. The system guarantees that heavy AI inference tasks (e.g., document parsing or multi-vendor scoring) do not block the user interface.

graph TD
    UI[Next.js Modern Web Interface] <-->|REST / WebSockets| GW[FastAPI API Gateway]

    subgraph Multi-Agent Orchestrator
        GW --> AO[Agent Pipeline Orchestrator]
        AO --> OCR[Document Intelligence Agent]
        AO --> INV[Inventory Analysis Agent]
        AO --> VEND[Vendor Evaluation Agent]
        AO --> RISK[Risk Assessment Agent]
        AO --> APPR[Approval Coordinator Agent]
        AO --> CHAT[RAG Vendor Chatbot Agent]
    end

    subgraph Messaging & Cache
        AO <-->|Events & Logs| KAFKA[Apache Kafka / Zookeeper]
        AO <-->|Session Cache / Fast State| REDIS[Redis Key-Value Cache]
    end

    subgraph Persistence Layer
        AO <-->|Relational Data| PG[(PostgreSQL Enterprise Database)]
        OCR <-->|PDF / Blob Storage| MINIO[(MinIO S3 Compatible Storage)]
    end

    subgraph External Connectors
        APPR -->|Digital Signature| DS[DocuSign API]
        AO -->|Alerts & PO Delivery| SMTP[Email / Notification Dispatcher]
        CHAT -->|LLM Queries| OPENAI[LLMs & Embedding Models]
    end

docs.title: ⚙️ Core Technology Stack
docs.text:
The system utilizes an enterprise stack tested for high throughput, data consistency, and low latency:

Layer Technologies Selected Justification & Purpose Frontend UI Next.js 14, React 18, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons High-performance server-side rendering, responsive responsive dashboard, real-time status indicators. Backend Services Python 3.10+, FastAPI, Pydantic, Uvicorn Asynchronous I/O, strict type validation, automated OpenAPI documentation generation. AI / Agentic Framework LangChain, OpenAI GPT-4 / Anthropic Claude, FAISS Vector Store Flexible agent tool-calling, chain-of-thought evaluation, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Message Streaming Apache Kafka & Zookeeper Asynchronous event streaming, distributed auditing, fault-tolerant message logging between microservices. Relational Database PostgreSQL 15 ACID transactional integrity, relational schema for POs, line items, and multi-tier approval logs. In-Memory Cache Redis 7 Caching active agent sessions, fast key-value lookups, rate limiting, and pub/sub messaging. Object Storage MinIO (S3-compatible) High-throughput object storage for invoices, vendor contracts, signed POs, and generated reports. Containerization Docker & Docker Compose Reproducible multi-service deployment, isolated networking, environment portability.

docs.title: 🔄 End-to-End Execution Flow
docs.text:
When a procurement trigger occurs (either by manual document upload or automated low-stock detection), execution traverses through coordinated agent stages:

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Manager as Procurement Manager
    participant UI as Next.js Web UI
    participant GW as FastAPI Gateway
    participant Orchestrator as Multi-Agent Core
    participant Kafka as Apache Kafka
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant DocuSign as DocuSign Integration

    Manager->>UI: Uploads Requisition / Invoice Document
    UI->>GW: POST /api/documents/upload
    GW->>Orchestrator: Ingest document into pipeline
    Orchestrator->>Kafka: Publish "DOCUMENT_UPLOADED" event

    rect rgb(30, 41, 59)
        Note over Orchestrator: OCR Agent parses tables & line items
        Note over Orchestrator: Inventory Agent detects stock deficit
        Note over Orchestrator: Vendor Agent ranks top 3 suppliers
        Note over Orchestrator: Risk Agent evaluates price variance & lead time
    end

    Orchestrator->>DB: Persist Draft Purchase Order & Recommendation
    Orchestrator->>Kafka: Publish "PO_AWAITING_APPROVAL" event
    UI->>Manager: Displays Actionable Approval Hub with Rationale
    Manager->>UI: Approves Order with Digital Signature
    UI->>DocuSign: Verify & Sign Final PO Document
    DocuSign-->>GW: Webhook "PO_EXECUTED"
    GW->>Kafka: Publish "PO_DISPATCHED"
    GW-->>Manager: Instant Confirmation & Audit Trail Updated

docs.title: 📊 System Execution Monitoring
docs.text: Every transaction produces real-time event logs delivered across Kafka topics. This provides complete visibility into: 1. Agent decision latency and execution duration. 2. Confidence scores and reasoning rationales for vendor selection. 3. Strict audit trails of who authorized financial expenditures.

docs.title: 🔒 Security Best Practices
docs.text: [!WARNING] Never commit .env or RSA private keys to version control. Ensure .env is listed in your .gitignore. For production deployments, consider injecting secrets via Docker Secrets, AWS Secrets Manager, or HashiCorp Vault.

docs.title: 1. Clone & Configure
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/ashleyworkbench/Multi-agent-procurement-system.git
cd Multi-agent-procurement-system
cp .env.example .env

docs.title: 2. Boot Infrastructure & Databases
docs.text:
You can boot the persistence and messaging layers first: 

docker compose -f docker-compose.databases.yml up -d

docs.title: 3. Launch Full System
docs.text:
docker compose up -d --build

Alternatively, use the convenience launch scripts:

Linux / macOSWindows PowerShellWindows CMD 
chmod +x start.sh
./start.sh

.\start.ps1

start.bat

docs.text:
Check that all containers are healthy:

Verify service connectivity:

curl -s http://localhost:8000/health | jq .

docs.title: 🌐 GitHub Pages Deployment for this Documentation
docs.text:
To host this documentation on GitHub Pages:

  2. In your GitHub repository settings, navigate to Settings > Pages.
  3. Under Build and deployment > Source, select GitHub Actions.
  4. The included .github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml will automatically build the site and publish it to: https://<your-username>.github.io/Multi-agent-procurement-system/

docs.title: Troubleshooting & FAQs
docs.text: This section addresses common deployment hurdles, service connectivity issues, port conflicts, and operational recovery steps.

docs.title: 1. Database Port Conflict (5432 or 6379 already in use)
docs.text:
• Symptom: Docker fails with Bind for 0.0.0.0:5432 failed: port is already allocated.
  • Cause: A local instance of PostgreSQL or Redis is running on the host machine.
  • Resolution: 
    # Check which process is using the port
sudo lsof -i :5432

# Stop the local host service
sudo systemctl stop postgresql
sudo systemctl stop redis-server

# Re-launch Docker containers
docker compose up -d

docs.title: 2. Kafka Connection Timeout (ConnectionRefusedError: [Errno 111])
docs.text:
• Symptom: FastAPI backend logs show connection retries to localhost:9092.
  • Cause: Kafka is still negotiating broker state with Zookeeper.
  • Resolution: Kafka requires approximately 10–15 seconds to complete cluster initialization on cold boot. Wait for the broker to announce readiness: 
    docker logs -f procureflow-kafka | grep -i "started"
    If restarting from a corrupted state: 
    docker compose stop kafka zookeeper
docker compose rm -f kafka zookeeper
docker compose up -d zookeeper kafka

docs.title: 3. MinIO S3 Bucket Missing Error (NoSuchBucket)
docs.text:
• Symptom: OCR file upload fails with 404 Bucket procureflow-documents does not exist.
  • Cause: MinIO initialized without running the bucket creation bootstrap.
  • Resolution: Access the MinIO Web Console at http://localhost:9001 (User: minioadmin / Pass: minioadmin) and manually create bucket procureflow-documents, or execute: 
    docker exec -it procureflow-minio mc alias set local http://localhost:9000 minioadmin minioadmin
docker exec -it procureflow-minio mc mb local/procureflow-documents

docs.title: 4. Complete System Reset & Database Rebuild
docs.text:
If you need to completely purge all containers, volumes, and cached tables to start from a clean slate:

Linux / macOSWindows PowerShell 
docker compose down -v
docker compose -f docker-compose.databases.yml up -d
python3 generate_vendor_seed_csvs.py
python3 seed_all_vendor_performance.py
docker compose up -d --build

.\rebuild-all.ps1

docs.title: ❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
docs.text:
Can ProcureFlow work without an active internet connection?

The core microservices, database, Kafka event bus, and rule-based vendor ranking can operate in an isolated intranet. However, external LLM calls (e.g. OpenAI GPT-4) and the DocuSign eSignature API require outbound HTTPS internet connectivity unless replaced with self-hosted open-weights models (e.g. Ollama / vLLM with Llama 3) and internal PKI signature certificates.

How is vendor scoring weighted?

The default scoring distribution is: - Price Competitiveness: 40% - Historical Delivery Punctuality: 30% - Quality & Defect Rate: 20% - Compliance & ESG Rating: 10%

Procurement administrators can adjust these weights per requisition in the Procurement Hub.

How does the system ensure agents don't make unauthorized purchases?

By strict architectural design, AI agents produce recommendations and drafts only. State transitions to PO_EXECUTED or PO_DISPATCHED can only be triggered by an authenticated human user via cryptographic signature or DocuSign authorization.

docs.title: Approvals, Governance & Digital Signatures
docs.text: ProcureFlow enforces enterprise-grade financial governance through role-based approval hierarchies and DocuSign digital signature integrations, guaranteeing that AI agents never dispatch funds or enter contracts autonomously without authorized human sign-off.

docs.title: 🏛️ Financial Approval Hierarchy
docs.text:
Every generated purchase order is evaluated against the organization's financial authority matrix:

Threshold Tier Order Value Required Approver Role Approval Mechanism Tier 1 (Operational) < $5,000 Procurement Specialist / Supervisor Single-click dashboard authorization Tier 2 (Managerial) $5,000 – $25,000 Department Head / Plant Manager Dashboard approval + Password confirmation Tier 3 (Executive) > $25,000 Director / Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Two-factor authorization + DocuSign Digital Signature

docs.title: 🎯 The Approval Hub & Recommendation Rationale
docs.text:
The Approval Hub provides approvers with full transparency into why a specific vendor and order quantity were selected:

Approvers can expand the Agent Decision Rationale to review: 1. Vendor scoring breakdown (price vs. quality vs. lead time). 2. Alternative vendors evaluated and why they were rejected. 3. Market risk index and lead-time volatility forecasts.

docs.title: ✍️ DocuSign & Cryptographic Signatures
docs.text: Once an executive approves an order, ProcureFlow automatically generates the legal PO contract and creates an envelope via the DocuSign eSignature API:

docs.title: Digital Signature Security Properties
docs.text:
• Cryptographic Hashing: The document content is hashed using SHA-256 prior to signature transmission.
  • Envelope Tracking: Real-time webhooks listen for envelope-signed and envelope-completed events.
  • Tamper Evidence: Once signed, any modification to the PO invalidates the certificate, preventing unauthorized modifications.
  • Audit Retention: The signed PDF and certificate of completion are stored securely in MinIO with links recorded in PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Document Intelligence & Optical Character Recognition (OCR)
docs.text:
In manufacturing procurement, documents such as vendor invoices, quotes, and bills of materials arrive in diverse, unstructured formats (scanned PDFs, PNG/JPEG receipts, and legacy spreadsheets).

The Document Intelligence Agent eliminates manual data entry by extracting, validating, and structuring line items into standardized JSON payloads.

docs.title: 📄 Ingestion Pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    DOC[Document Upload PDF/Image] --> VAL[File Validation & MIME Check]
    VAL --> MINIO[(Store in MinIO Bucket)]
    VAL --> OCR_ENGINE[OCR Preprocessing & Binarization]
    OCR_ENGINE --> LLM_EXTRACT[LLM Vision & Structured Parser]
    LLM_EXTRACT --> SCHEMA_VAL[Pydantic Schema Validation]
    SCHEMA_VAL --> EXTRACTED[(Extracted Line Items Store)]

docs.text:
The system supports drag-and-drop document upload with real-time feedback:

Once processed, the agent displays a comprehensive line-item summary with confidence indicators for each extracted field:

docs.title: 🔍 Structured Extraction Schema
docs.text:
Extracted data is normalized into strict Pydantic models:

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import List, Optional

class ExtractedLineItem(BaseModel):
    item_description: str = Field(description="Name or description of raw material/component")
    part_number: Optional[str] = Field(description="Manufacturer SKU or internal part code")
    quantity: float = Field(description="Quantity requested or invoiced")
    unit_of_measure: str = Field(description="Units (e.g., pcs, kg, meters, liters)")
    unit_price: float = Field(description="Quoted price per unit")
    total_amount: float = Field(description="Calculated total price for line item")
    confidence_score: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0, description="OCR extraction certainty")

class ParsedDocumentResponse(BaseModel):
    document_id: str
    vendor_name: Optional[str]
    invoice_date: Optional[str]
    currency: str = "USD"
    subtotal: float
    tax_amount: float
    total_amount: float
    line_items: List[ExtractedLineItem]

docs.title: 🛡️ Error Handling & Fallbacks
docs.text:
• Low-Confidence Flags: Any field extracted with a confidence score below 0.80 is highlighted in yellow for manual verification.
  • Mathematical Reconciliation: The agent validates that $\sum (\text{Quantity} \times \text{Unit Price}) + \text{Tax} = \text{Total Amount}$. Any discrepancies trigger an instant mismatch alert before passing data to the downstream Inventory Agent.

docs.title: End-to-End Procurement Lifecycle
docs.text: ProcureFlow transforms the multi-step manufacturing procurement process into a seamless, autonomous, and auditable pipeline.

docs.title: 🔄 End-to-End Workflow Stages
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[1. Ingestion / Requisition] --> B[2. Stock Shortage Analysis]
    B --> C[3. Multi-Criteria Vendor Evaluation]
    C --> D[4. Composite Risk Scoring]
    D --> E[5. Human-in-the-Loop Approval]
    E --> F[6. Digital Signature & PO Generation]
    F --> G[7. Vendor Dispatch & Tracking]

docs.title: 1. Ingestion & Trigger
docs.text:
• A user uploads a requisition file, bill of materials (BOM), or invoice.
  • Alternatively, automated database triggers flag items that drop below their Safety Stock limit.

docs.title: 2. Autonomous Deficit Analysis
docs.text:
• The Inventory Analysis Agent queries real-time stock across multiple warehouse databases.
  • The agent calculates exact deficit quantities, lead times, and urgency classifications (e.g., Critical, Standard, Low Priority).

docs.title: 3. Dynamic Vendor Scoring & Evaluation
docs.text:
• The Vendor Evaluation Agent calculates a composite score for qualified suppliers based on:
  • Unit Price competitiveness
  • Historical delivery punctuality
  • Defect and return rate
  • ESG and compliance certifications

docs.title: 4. Risk Mitigation & Sanity Checks
docs.text:
• The Risk Assessment Agent examines market price fluctuations, geopolitical supplier dependencies, and delivery reliability.
  • Recommendations are accompanied by clear reasoning rationales.

docs.title: 5. Tiered Managerial Approval
docs.text:
• Orders passing all automated checks are routed according to predefined financial thresholds.
  • Managers review the consolidated dashboard and approve or reject with single-click actions.

docs.title: 6. PO Execution & Signature
docs.text:
• Upon approval, the system generates an official PDF Purchase Order with an immutable cryptographic hash.
  • Integrates directly with DocuSign for legally binding digital signatures.

docs.title: ⏱️ Real-Time Workflow Tracking
docs.text: ProcureFlow features a dedicated Workflow Tracker providing real-time visibility into the lifecycle of every requisition and agent execution state.

docs.title: 📈 Operational Efficiency Gains
docs.text: Compared to traditional manual manufacturing procurement: - Processing Time: Reduced from 3–5 business days to under 4 minutes. - Data Entry Errors: Cut by 98% through automated document OCR and schema validation. - Spend Optimization: Up to 12% average cost savings via dynamic multi-vendor price comparison.
